We have added a Vendor IP/law/data-breach/misconduct indemnity per our playbook.","confidence":0.86,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0080","oldText":"Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.","newText":"Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

21.5 Indemnification. Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Customer shall give Vendor prompt notice of the claim, and Vendor shall have control of the defence and settlement (provided no settlement imposing liability or admission on Customer is made without Customer's consent), with Customer's reasonable cooperation at Vendor's expense. For an infringement claim, Vendor shall at its expense procure the right to continue use, or modify or replace the affected item so it is non-infringing and materially equivalent, failing which Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of prepaid Fees. Customer shall indemnify Vendor only against third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.","comment":"[Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity at all, yet Section 9.3 references "Section 20.5" and the cap carves out indemnification obligations. We have inserted our standard Vendor indemnity (IP, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with the usual notice-and-control procedure, and kept Customer's indemnity narrow."}},{"ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","status":"deviation","paragraphIds":["p0046","p0044"],"quote":"During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","rationale":"An undefined, worldwide, 24-month post-term non-compete on Customer is a walk-away item and directly contradicts Section 12.3, which confirms Customer has made no non-compete commitment. If some protection is genuinely needed, we could consider a restriction limited to one named competing product, during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions."}},{"ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0044"],"quote":"Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Customer; Section 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to engage other suppliers.","confidence":0.85},{"ruleId":"MFN","status":"deviation","paragraphIds":["p0026"],"quote":"Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.","rationale":"This is an open-ended MFN running in the Vendor's favour, obliging us to disclose and match third-party offers — our walk-away position, and inconsistent with Section 12.3. MFN pricing in our favour would of course be welcome."}},{"ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","status":"deviation","paragraphIds":["p0045"],"quote":"Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","rationale":"This is a 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out — our walk-away position. We have narrowed it to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services, with the standard carve-outs.","confidence":0.93,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0045","oldText":"12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","newText":"12.4 During the term and for twelve months after the end of an individual's involvement in the Services, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment any personnel of the other Party who were directly involved in the Services. This restriction does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment not targeted at such personnel, or to unsolicited approaches by the individual, and neither Party is prohibited from hiring any person who responds to such recruitment or approach.","comment":"[Playbook] We accept only a narrow, mutual, time-limited non-solicit: personnel actually involved in the Services, 12 months, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. No-hire language must come out."}},{"ruleId":"T4C","status":"missing","paragraphIds":["p0032","p0036","p0039"],"quote":"This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms.","rationale":"Section 9 gives termination rights only for breach, insolvency and Vendor performance failures; there is no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a three-year term. We have added a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees.","confidence":0.88,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0039","oldText":"A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.","newText":"A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

9.6 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and Customer shall have no further payment obligation for the terminated Services. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.","comment":"[Playbook] In a three-year term we need a convenience exit: 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. If a notice period is an issue, we can move to 60 days, but the right itself is not negotiable."}},{"ruleId":"RENEWAL","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0033","p0034"],"quote":"renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal","rationale":"12-month renewals, a 30-day opt-out window, a 60-day Vendor reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% all match our preferred position.","confidence":0.92},{"ruleId":"GOVLAW","status":"deviation","paragraphIds":["p0103","p0104"],"quote":"28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.","rationale":"Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue is outside our accepted list and also contradicts Section 28.2, which vests exclusive jurisdiction in the New York County courts. We have moved governing law to New York to align with Section 28.2.","confidence":0.94,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0103","oldText":"28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.","newText":"28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.","comment":"[Playbook] Our accepted jurisdictions are New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales. New York also matches the exclusive venue already agreed in Section 28.2 and both parties' places of business."}},{"ruleId":"ASSIGN","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0087","p0088","p0090"],"quote":"Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.","rationale":"Customer has an affiliate/successor assignment right without consent, Vendor assignment requires our consent and is barred to competitors, and no Vendor right arises on our change of control. We have reversed the ownership direction, leaving Vendor Technology with Vendor.","confidence":0.93,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0054","oldText":"14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3, and Customer's rights in embedded Vendor Technology are as set out in Section 13.2.","comment":"[Playbook] We own the work product we pay for; the Vendor keeps its pre-existing platform and tools. Note that the take-or-pay commitment in Section 2.1 is addressed separately under our minimum-commitment position.","confidence":0.78},{"ruleId":"WARRANTY","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0071","p0072","p0074","p0075"],"quote":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria.","rationale":"Professional-services warranty, 90-day Deliverable conformance (hosted Services for the whole term), repair/re-perform/replace/refund remedy, compliance with law and no-malicious-code, and a disclaimer that does not swallow the express warranties.","confidence":0.9},{"ruleId":"INSURANCE","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0068","p0069"],"quote":"commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000","rationale":"Coverage lines and limits meet or exceed our preferred position, with certificates on request and no limitation of liability by reference to insurance.","confidence":0.95},{"ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","status":"deviation","paragraphIds":["p0012","p0044"],"quote":"Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"A three-year, USD 6M take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right is our walk-away position and contradicts Section 12.3's confirmation that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. Any minimum purchase commitment stated in an Order Form is limited to the then-current twelve-month term, may be reduced by Customer on thirty days' written notice, and any shortfall will be settled as a true-up of Fees for Services actually ordered rather than as a penalty or take-or-pay amount.","comment":"[Playbook] We do not accept multi-year take-or-pay without an exit. We have inserted the standard exit provision.","confidence":0.85,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0042","oldText":"Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","newText":"Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

10.3 On expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for export all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems, subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements, and certify such deletion in writing.","comment":"[Playbook] On exit we need our data back in a usable format and help migrating. We have added six months of transition assistance at your then-current rates, a 30-day data-return obligation and certified deletion; this also fixes the broken cross-reference to "Section 11" in Section 16.5."}}]}

findings.quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000.
findings.rationale: Mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, mutual damages exclusion, and the full set of uncapped Excluded Claims. Matches our preferred position; no change needed.

findings.quote: infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5
findings.rationale: There is no indemnification section in the Agreement, although Section 9.3 cross-refers to "Section 20.5" and the liability cap carves out "its indemnification obligations" — so the drafting assumes an indemnity that is missing. We have added a Vendor IP/law/data-breach/misconduct indemnity per our playbook.

replacement.oldText: Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.
replacement.newText:
Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

21.5 Indemnification. Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Customer shall give Vendor prompt notice of the claim, and Vendor shall have control of the defence and settlement (provided no settlement imposing liability or admission on Customer is made without Customer's consent), with Customer's reasonable cooperation at Vendor's expense. For an infringement claim, Vendor shall at its expense procure the right to continue use, or modify or replace the affected item so it is non-infringing and materially equivalent, failing which Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of prepaid Fees. Customer shall indemnify Vendor only against third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity at all, yet Section 9.3 references "Section 20.5" and the cap carves out indemnification obligations. We have inserted our standard Vendor indemnity (IP, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with the usual notice-and-control procedure, and kept Customer's indemnity narrow.

findings.quote: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
findings.rationale: An undefined, worldwide, 24-month post-term non-compete on Customer is a walk-away item and directly contradicts Section 12.3, which confirms Customer has made no non-compete commitment. We have deleted it.

replacement.oldText: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We cannot restrict the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build, and this clause also conflicts with Section 12.3. If some protection is genuinely needed, we could consider a restriction limited to one named competing product, during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.

findings.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
findings.rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Customer; Section 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to engage other suppliers.

findings.quote: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
findings.rationale: This is an open-ended MFN running in the Vendor's favour, obliging us to disclose and match third-party offers — our walk-away position, and inconsistent with Section 12.3. We have deleted it.

replacement.oldText: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept MFN obligations running in the Vendor's favour or any duty to disclose or match third-party offers. MFN pricing in our favour would of course be welcome.

findings.quote: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
findings.rationale: This is a 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out — our walk-away position. We have narrowed it to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services, with the standard carve-outs.

replacement.oldText: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
replacement.newText: 12.4 During the term and for twelve months after the end of an individual's involvement in the Services, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment any personnel of the other Party who were directly involved in the Services. This restriction does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment not targeted at such personnel, or to unsolicited approaches by the individual, and neither Party is prohibited from hiring any person who responds to such recruitment or approach.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We accept only a narrow, mutual, time-limited non-solicit: personnel actually involved in the Services, 12 months, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. No-hire language must come out.

findings.quote: This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms.
findings.rationale: Section 9 gives termination rights only for breach, insolvency and Vendor performance failures; there is no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a three-year term. We have added a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees.

replacement.oldText: A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
replacement.newText:
A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

9.6 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and Customer shall have no further payment obligation for the terminated Services. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] In a three-year term we need a convenience exit: 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. If a notice period is an issue, we can move to 60 days, but the right itself is not negotiable.

findings.quote: renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal
findings.rationale: 12-month renewals, a 30-day opt-out window, a 60-day Vendor reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% all match our preferred position.

findings.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
findings.rationale: Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue is outside our accepted list and also contradicts Section 28.2, which vests exclusive jurisdiction in the New York County courts. We have moved governing law to New York to align with Section 28.2.

replacement.oldText: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
replacement.newText: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] Our accepted jurisdictions are New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales. New York also matches the exclusive venue already agreed in Section 28.2 and both parties' places of business.

findings.quote: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.
findings.rationale: Customer has an affiliate/successor assignment right without consent, Vendor assignment requires our consent and is barred to competitors, and no Vendor right arises on our change of control. Matches our preferred position.

findings.quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
findings.rationale: We must own the Deliverables we pay to have created, and a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence is our walk-away position (it also conflicts with the perpetual licence contemplated in Sections 13.2 and 14.3). We have reversed the ownership direction, leaving Vendor Technology with Vendor.

replacement.oldText: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
replacement.newText: 14.2 Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title and interest, including all intellectual property rights, in each Deliverable. Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3, and Customer's rights in embedded Vendor Technology are as set out in Section 13.2.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for; the Vendor keeps its pre-existing platform and tools. As drafted, the revocable term licence is inconsistent with the perpetual licence in Sections 13.2 and 14.3. If assignment is impossible, the minimum is a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify the Deliverables.

findings.quote: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right
findings.rationale: Affiliates and contractors are covered, paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable, transfer to a successor is permitted, and revocation is limited to uncured material breach.

findings.quote: no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice
findings.rationale: Annual frequency, 30 days' notice, off-site independent auditor, Vendor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct system access — matches our preferred position.

findings.quote: Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.
findings.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalties or termination penalties are payable by Customer. Note that the take-or-pay commitment in Section 2.1 is addressed separately under our minimum-commitment position.

findings.quote: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria.
findings.rationale: Professional-services warranty, 90-day Deliverable conformance (hosted Services for the whole term), repair/re-perform/replace/refund remedy, compliance with law and no-malicious-code, and a disclaimer that does not swallow the express warranties.

findings.quote: commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000
findings.rationale: Coverage lines and limits meet or exceed our preferred position, with certificates on request and no limitation of liability by reference to insurance.

findings.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
findings.rationale: A three-year, USD 6M take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right is our walk-away position and contradicts Section 12.3's confirmation that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. We have narrowed it to a 12-month, reducible commitment settled by true-up.

replacement.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
replacement.newText: 2.1 Customer may order Services under Order Forms from time to time. Any minimum purchase commitment stated in an Order Form is limited to the then-current twelve-month term, may be reduced by Customer on thirty days' written notice, and any shortfall will be settled as a true-up of Fees for Services actually ordered rather than as a penalty or take-or-pay amount.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept multi-year take-or-pay without an exit. Our fallback is a commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up instead of a penalty; the clause as drafted also conflicts with Section 12.3.

findings.quote: Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
findings.rationale: Section 10 addresses Deliverables and refunds but contains no transition assistance, no Customer Data return in a machine-readable format, and no deletion/certification timing (Section 16.5 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 11). We have inserted the standard exit provision.

replacement.oldText: Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
replacement.newText:
Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

10.3 On expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for export all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems, subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements, and certify such deletion in writing.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] On exit we need our data back in a usable format and help migrating. We have added six months of transition assistance at your then-current rates, a 30-day data-return obligation and certified deletion; this also fixes the broken cross-reference to "Section 11" in Section 16.5.
